request.spec:
A crew is now also a pool: it appears among the pools under its name, with the lead and the
members as its members at equal shares (100.00 split as patrons' shares are, the remainder on the
lead), and receives cuts like any pool. A pool cannot be added with a crew's name nor a crew with a
pool's name. Crew totals stay as they are.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A crew is now also a pool: it appears among the pools under its name, with the lead and the
members as its members at equal shares (100.00 split as patrons' shares are, the remainder on the
lead), and receives cuts like any pool. A pool cannot be added with a crew's name nor a crew with a
pool's name. Crew totals stay as they are.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Crews now show up as pools. Two of the four tests pass: the main "crews are pools" test and scenario 2. Scenarios 1 and 3 still fail. Both stop on steps that don't involve crews or pools, before reaching anything that does.

**What changed**
- **Pools list** (`pool/RespondWithPools.java`): after the stored pools, each crew is listed as a pool under its own name. Its members are the lead, then the crew members in the order added. 100.00 is split among them the way patrons' shares are, with the remainder on the lead (so 33.34 / 33.33 / 33.33). They get cuts of the sheet's pot like any pool, and held or retired members are handled the same way. The share split is `PoolResponse.equalShares`, and each crew pool carries a `crewId`.
- **Name clashes**: adding a pool with a crew's name is refused (`SavePool`), and so is adding a crew with a pool's name (`SaveCrew`). Either refusal shows the usual form error and writes nothing.
- **Front end** (`features/pools/`): a crew's pool has no "add member" form, since its members come from the crew. Crew pools also aren't offered when choosing a pool to add as a member. Crew rows and crew totals are unchanged.
- No database migration was needed: crew pools are built from the existing crew tables each time the pools are listed.

**The two failing tests**
- **Scenario 3** (line 1430) can't pass. The spec expects the sheet's parent to read literally `"__SHEET__-p"`, which looks like a placeholder that was never filled in. The app correctly shows the real sheet id (e.g. `smvkobomp0w47-p`).
- **Scenario 1** (line 128) expects pasting `Ben,20.00,,` and `Ben,7.77,2026-03-20,` to add 3 claims. Line 2's blank date defaults to today, 2026-03-20, so line 3 has the same date and blank note as the claim line 2 just created and opened. The current paste rule (documented in `PasteClaims.java` and `paste-claims.POST.yml`) refuses a line that matches a non-draft claim, so the whole paste is rejected. Making this pass would mean changing the rule so a line only matches claims that existed before the paste. That's outside this request, so I haven't done it; tell me if you want it.

**Running the tests:** your environment sets `PORT=3002`, and another process is already listening there, so plain `bin/e2e` fails to start the app. I didn't touch that process and ran the tests with `PORT=3417 bin/e2e` instead.
